passages.text: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks in this passage.
She loves a man deeply.
She lies on her bed at night.
She searches for the one she loves.
She looks for him.
She does not find him.
passages.original: עַל־ מִשְׁכָּבִי֙ בַּלֵּיל֔וֹת בִּקַּ֕שְׁתִּי אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א מְצָאתִֽיו׃

passages.text: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks in this passage.
She loves a man deeply.
She cannot find him.
She decides to get up now.
She will go around the city.
She will walk through the streets.
She will go through the squares.
She will look for the one she loves.
She searches for him.
She does not find him.
passages.original: אָק֨וּמָה נָּ֜א וַאֲסוֹבְבָ֣ה בָעִ֗יר בַּשְּׁוָקִים֙ וּבָ֣רְחֹב֔וֹת אֲבַקְשָׁ֕ה אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א מְצָאתִֽיו׃

passages.text: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”
passages.sermon:
The woman searched for her beloved in the city.
She met the watchmen who walked around the city.
She spoke to the watchmen.
She asked them, “Have you seen the one I love?”
passages.original: מְצָא֙וּנִי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים הַסֹּבְבִ֖ים בָּעִ֑יר אֵ֛ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י רְאִיתֶֽם׃

passages.text: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.
passages.sermon:
A woman searched for the one she loved.
She had just passed the watchmen in the city.
Then she found the one she loved.
She held him tightly.
She refused to let him go.
She brought him to her mother’s house.
She brought him to the room where her mother had conceived her.
passages.original: כִּמְעַט֙ שֶׁעָבַ֣רְתִּי מֵהֶ֔ם עַ֣ד שֶֽׁמָּצָ֔אתִי אֵ֥ת שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י אֲחַזְתִּיו֙ וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֔נּוּ עַד־ שֶׁ֤הֲבֵיאתִיו֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית אִמִּ֔י וְאֶל־ חֶ֖דֶר הוֹרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the daughters of Jerusalem.
The speaker gives them a solemn warning.
The speaker calls on the gazelles and the does of the field as witnesses.
The speaker says, “Do not arouse love.”
The speaker says, “Do not awaken love.”
The speaker says, “Wait until love desires to be awakened.”
The speaker warns them not to force love before its proper time.
passages.original: הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה אִם־ תָּעִ֧ירוּ׀ וְֽאִם־ תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ אֶת־ הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ס

passages.text: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?
passages.sermon:
A person is coming up from the wilderness.
This person rises like a column of smoke.
The smoke carries the scent of myrrh and frankincense.
The scent comes from all the spices of the merchant.
passages.original: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן־ הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר כְּתִֽימֲר֖וֹת עָשָׁ֑ן מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת מוֹר֙ וּלְבוֹנָ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל אַבְקַ֥ת רוֹכֵֽל׃

passages.text: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon is the subject.
He has a carriage.
Sixty mighty men of Israel surround his carriage.
These men escort the carriage.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֗ה מִטָּתוֹ֙ שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שִׁשִּׁ֥ים גִּבֹּרִ֖ים סָבִ֣יב לָ֑הּ מִגִּבֹּרֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.
passages.sermon:
These men are mighty warriors of Israel.
Each man holds a sword.
Each man knows how to fight in battle.
Each man keeps his sword at his side.
Each man is ready to face danger at night.
passages.original: כֻּלָּם֙ אֲחֻ֣זֵי חֶ֔רֶב מְלֻמְּדֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה אִ֤ישׁ חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל־ יְרֵכ֔וֹ מִפַּ֖חַד בַּלֵּילּֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.
passages.sermon: King Solomon is the king of Israel.\r\nKing Solomon made a carriage for himself.\r\nHe used timber from Lebanon to build the carriage.
passages.original: אַפִּרְי֗וֹן עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵעֲצֵ֖י הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃

passages.text: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made a carriage.
He made its posts from silver.
He made its base from gold.
He made its seat from purple fabric.
The daughters of Jerusalem inlaid its interior with love.
passages.original: עַמּוּדָיו֙ עָ֣שָׂה כֶ֔סֶף רְפִידָת֣וֹ זָהָ֔ב מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ אַרְגָּמָ֑ן תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown his mother bestowed on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon is the king of Israel.
His mother gave him a crown.
She gave it to him on his wedding day.
That day was the day of his great joy.
Daughters of Zion, come out.
Look at King Solomon wearing his crown.
passages.original: צְאֶ֧ינָה׀ וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בָּעֲטָרָ֗ה שֶׁעִטְּרָה־ לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ בְּי֣וֹם חֲתֻנָּת֔וֹ וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃ס
